reasons: Deviation is correctly identified: the § 12.1 grant is expressly 'revocable' with no standard and runs only to 'Customer', matching the rule's detection cues (revocable grant, affiliates/contractors unnamed).

Redline reaches the playbook position: it adds Affiliates and contractors acting on Customer's behalf, deletes 'revocable', and ties cessation of the licence to expiration/termination under Section 3 rather than Vendor discretion.
Successor transfer is reasonably not re-added because § 14.10 already permits assignment to a successor by merger/consolidation/acquisition, keeping the edit minimal.

The failed 'minimal edit' heuristic (ratio 0.689) is explained by the necessary added sentence replacing the at-will revocation right; the original operative restrictions (copying/reverse engineering) and 'solely in connection with the Services' limitation are preserved.
Comment is accurate, in-house tone, states what changed and why, and offers the affiliates-on-written-notice fallback.

Minor: the rationale asserts 'Affiliates' is defined in the preamble but the resolved definitions only show 'Customer'; if no such definition exists, the term should be defined or replaced with a descriptive phrase (e.g., entities controlled by Customer).
